frozen_before_participants.uniform_rag_version: Initial eight-task RAG source restored after rejected direct-member candidate. All eight exact saved inputs/results reused; no choosing best answer.
frozen_before_participants.scope: Fresh developer participants, previously revealed known-repository tasks. Actual source-grounded final integration decisions and extra source acquisition measured; no new task generalization or human time estimate.
frozen_before_participants.carryover: Two tasks per known repository per developer; separated environments prohibit cross-task source copying, but within-repository learning/order effects cannot be excluded.

study_design.objective: Improve SDK integration decision completion and the developer effort needed to establish trustworthy conclusions, using the existing model and retrieval/tool modules.

question_design.selection: Authors inspect fixed source and prior question text, without inspecting new retrieval results or model answers; exclude duplicated mechanisms and earlier repair cases. Known repositories, new tasks; not unseen-repository or production distribution evidence.
question_design.required_points: Only explicit business decisions, normally 3-4 per task; alternate valid implementation advice and supporting sources accepted. Tests are required only if asked.
question_design.split: business-confirmation; revealed questions remain development-only afterward; original final-test repositories stay sealed; no training.

same_fields: output allowance and total context window
fixed_comparison.baseline: Existing fixed identifier-location heuristic and bounded source reads; not an adaptive developer or universal code-search baseline. Original helper defaults remain 4KB/3; this study explicitly matches 8KB/6.
report: strict completion of frozen business decisions
fixed_comparison.truth_and_input: Reference answers never enter retrieval selection or model messages. Generated source windows and citations verified against immutable snapshot.

agent_probe.selection: One HTTP/web and one config/events integration task chosen by ID before any model generation; same question and initial RAG context.
agent_probe.interpretation: Pipeline utility versus fixed RAG at observed additional cost, not a pure tool-permission causal ablation or independent extra task count.

conditions: actual RAG answer plus its delivered raw sources, with same further source tools
developer_trial.assignment: Each developer receives one RAG-assisted and one direct-reading task in each repository; the second developer receives the complementary assignment. Task order frozen and counterbalanced; no developer sees the same task in both modes.
developer_trial.tool_backend: RepositoryEnvironment with plain BM25 code_aware=False for both modes; restored states retain exact visible source and tool trace. No gold files, benchmark summaries, web search, target-code execution, or further generator calls.
developer_trial.final_deliverable: Concrete integration decision, recommended adjustment where needed, supporting source line citations, and unresolved gaps; use standard answer/citations/insufficient_evidence contract.
developer_trial.primary_business_outcome: Independent source-grounded decision completion and severe errors, plus actual additional source tool calls and delivered bytes.
developer_trial.efficiency_reporting: Report measured source acquisition/verification operations on these tasks; no inferred human time savings, production adoption or revenue. Wall-clock logs are descriptive and affected by agent scheduling.

review.reviewers: Task authors judge anonymous generated and developer answers against frozen necessary business points and actual visible sources; separate original judgments and amendments.
review.judgment: Existing semantic_review.validate_judgment; workflow success alone is insufficient.

optimization_gate.purpose: Only a general, bounded change in existing code motivated by a concrete missing or mishandled source; sufficiently visible source misunderstood by generator is not labelled a retrieval failure.
optimization_gate.adopt: At least one additional business task strictly completed with no previously completed task lost or new severe factual/business error; inspect all changed new-task inputs and reuse unchanged saved protection inputs. Preserve original first-confirmation scores.
optimization_gate.stop: Reject if source sufficiency or correctness gate fails; do not stack per-question prompts, modules, alternate models or repeated variants.

generator_limit.later_candidate: Only if failure-supported purpose; freeze a separate small plan before new requests. No automatic retries.

study_design.code_scope: No new runtime module or agent loop. Existing baseline helper and benchmark receive only the wiring needed for matched-budget comparison. Daily RAG/SDK source selection and model configuration are unchanged at first confirmation.

protocol.scope: Two fresh developer participants each complete eight revealed business workflows. Complementary task assignment; each sees one mode per question, one assisted and one direct per repository. Primary outcome is final source-grounded integration decisions and extra tool/byte acquisition. Model-assisted task performance, not human approval, production adoption or monetary/time savings. Within-repository learning, small sample, participant and order effects remain.
protocol.trial_source: Private bundles/states retain actual source observations; dataset/results/summary/manifests are the reviewable retained evidence.
protocol.presentation_followup: An empty final_context SDK failure edge was fixed after trial started; none of these eight fixed RAG records has that shape, all assisted delivered Markdown remains exact.

def blueprint(self) -> str | None:
        """The registered name of the current blueprint.

        This will be ``None`` if the endpoint is not part of a
        blueprint, or if URL matching failed or has not been performed
        yet.

        This does not necessarily match the name the blueprint was
        created with. It may have been nested, or registered with a
        different name.
        """
        endpoint = self.endpoint

        if endpoint is not None and "." in endpoint:
            return endpoint.rpartition(".")[0]

        return None

    @property
    def blueprints(self) -> list[str]:
        """The registered names of the current blueprint upwards through
        parent blueprints.

        This will be an empty list if there is no current blueprint, or
        if URL matching failed.

        .. versionadded:: 2.0.1
        """
        name = self.blueprint

        if name is None:
            return []

def _walk_to_root(path: str) -> Iterator[str]:
    """
    Yield directories starting from the given directory up to the root
    """
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        raise IOError("Starting path not found")

    if os.path.isfile(path):
        path = os.path.dirname(path)

    last_dir = None
    current_dir = os.path.abspath(path)
    while last_dir != current_dir:
        yield current_dir
        parent_dir = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(current_dir, os.path.pardir))
        last_dir, current_dir = current_dir, parent_dir

from .base import ANY
from .base import default_namespace
from .base import NamedSignal
from .base import Namespace
from .base import Signal
from .base import signal

def connect(self, receiver: F, sender: t.Any = ANY, weak: bool = True) -> F:
        """Connect ``receiver`` to be called when the signal is sent by
        ``sender``.

        :param receiver: The callable to call when :meth:`send` is called with
            the given ``sender``, passing ``sender`` as a positional argument
            along with any extra keyword arguments.
        :param sender: Any object or :data:`ANY`. ``receiver`` will only be
            called when :meth:`send` is called with this sender. If ``ANY``, the
            receiver will be called for any sender. A receiver may be connected
            to multiple senders by calling :meth:`connect` multiple times.
        :param weak: Track the receiver with a :mod:`weakref`. The receiver will
            be automatically disconnected when it is garbage collected. When
            connecting a receiver defined within a function, set to ``False``,
            otherwise it will be disconnected when the function scope ends.
        """
        receiver_id = make_id(receiver)
        sender_id = ANY_ID if sender is ANY else make_id(sender)

        if weak:
            self.receivers[receiver_id] = make_ref(
                receiver, self._make_cleanup_receiver(receiver_id)
            )
        else:
            self.receivers[receiver_id] = receiver

        self._by_sender[sender_id].add(receiver_id)
        self._by_receiver[receiver_id].add(sender_id)

def send(
        self,
        sender: t.Any | None = None,
        /,
        *,
        _async_wrapper: c.Callable[
            [c.Callable[..., c.Coroutine[t.Any, t.Any, t.Any]]], c.Callable[..., t.Any]
        ]
        | None = None,
        **kwargs: t.Any,
    ) -> list[tuple[c.Callable[..., t.Any], t.Any]]:
        """Call all receivers that are connected to the given ``sender``
        or :data:`ANY`. Each receiver is called with ``sender`` as a positional
        argument along with any extra keyword arguments. Return a list of
        ``(receiver, return value)`` tuples.

        The order receivers are called is undefined, but can be influenced by
        setting :attr:`set_class`.

        If a receiver raises an exception, that exception will propagate up.
        This makes debugging straightforward, with an assumption that correctly
        implemented receivers will not raise.

        :param sender: Call receivers connected to this sender, in addition to
            those connected to :data:`ANY`.
        :param _async_wrapper: Will be called on any receivers that are async
            coroutines to turn them into sync callables. For example, could run
            the receiver with an event loop.
        :param kwargs: Extra keyword arguments to pass to each receiver.

        .. versionchanged:: 1.7
            Added the ``_async_wrapper`` argument.
        """
        if self.is_muted:
            return []

        results = []

        for receiver in self.receivers_for(sender):
            if iscoroutinefunction(receiver):
                if _async_wrapper is None:
                    raise RuntimeError("Cannot send to a coroutine function.")

                result = _async_wrapper(receiver)(sender, **kwargs)
            else:
                result = receiver(sender, **kwargs)

            results.append((receiver, result))

        return results

class Namespace(dict[str, NamedSignal]):
    """A dict mapping names to signals."""

    def signal(self, name: str, doc: str | None = None) -> NamedSignal:
        """Return the :class:`NamedSignal` for the given ``name``, creating it
        if required. Repeated calls with the same name return the same signal.

        :param name: The name of the signal.
        :param doc: The docstring of the signal.
        """
        if name not in self:
            self[name] = NamedSignal(name, doc)

        return self[name]


class _PNamespaceSignal(t.Protocol):
    def __call__(self, name: str, doc: str | None = None) -> NamedSignal: ...


default_namespace: Namespace = Namespace()
"""A default :class:`Namespace` for creating named signals. :func:`signal`
creates a :class:`NamedSignal` in this namespace.
"""

signal: _PNamespaceSignal = default_namespace.signal
"""Return a :class:`NamedSignal` in :data:`default_namespace` with the given
``name``, creating it if required. Repeated calls with the same name return the
same signal.
"""

@contextmanager
    def muted(self) -> c.Generator[None, None, None]:
        """A context manager that temporarily disables the signal. No receivers
        will be called if the signal is sent, until the ``with`` block exits.
        Useful for tests.
        """
        self.is_muted = True

        try:
            yield None
        finally:
            self.is_muted = False

    def send(
        self,
        sender: t.Any | None = None,
        /,
        *,
        _async_wrapper: c.Callable[
            [c.Callable[..., c.Coroutine[t.Any, t.Any, t.Any]]], c.Callable[..., t.Any]
        ]

    ) -> list[tuple[c.Callable[..., t.Any], t.Any]]:

        The order receivers are called is undefined, but can be influenced by
        setting :attr:`set_class`.

        :param kwargs: Extra keyword arguments to pass to each receiver.

    def received(sender: t.Any) -> None:
        sentinel.append(sender)
